1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement (optionally with one equi-join)
8	  against a table-name to path mapping
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Without
45	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
46	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
47	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
48	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
49	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
50	
51	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
52	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
53	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
54	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
55	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
56	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
57	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
58	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
59	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
60	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
61	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
62	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
63	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
64	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
65	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
66	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
67	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection.  ORDER BY
68	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
69	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
70	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
71	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
72	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
73	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
74	
75	Searched CASE expressions
76	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
77	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
78	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
79	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
80	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
81	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
82	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
83	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
84	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
85	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
86	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
87	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
88	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
89	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
90	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
91	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
92	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
93	expressions.
94	
95	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
96	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
97	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
98	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
99	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
100	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
101	
102	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
103	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
104	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
105	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
106	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
107	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
108	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
109	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
110	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
111	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
112	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
113	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
114	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
115	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
116	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
117	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
118	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
119	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
120	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
121	
122	Two-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add one equi-join to the grammar::
123	
124	    query := SELECT ... FROM left_table [join_kind JOIN right_table
125	             ON left_table.column = right_table.column] ...
126	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT
127	
128	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
129	the statement are read.  Aliases, compound ON conditions, other join types
130	and a second join are rejected as syntax errors before any file is opened.
131	In a join query every column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be
132	qualified as ``table.column`` (either part may be a double-quoted
133	identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the left schema followed by the right
134	schema with ``table.column`` names; explicit projections keep their
135	qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase ``FUNC(table.column)``
136	labels.  Join keys may share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys
137	never match.  INNER JOIN emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also
138	emits unmatched left rows with the right-side values set to NULL (the
139	right result columns are nullable).  Rows expand in left-file order, and
140	within one left row in right-file order, before WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING
141	/ ORDER BY / LIMIT apply with their usual semantics.
142	
143	The multi-file entry points (:func:`query_files`, :func:`explain_files`)
144	take an optional ``join_strategy`` of ``"hash"`` or ``"sort_merge"``.
145	Both strategies accept the same statements and return identical column
146	descriptions, values, NULL placement and row order; they differ only in
147	how matching right rows are located (a right-key hash index versus
148	sorting both sides on the key and merging equal-key runs).  With the
149	argument omitted the historical join path is used and the explain plan
150	is unchanged; with an explicit strategy the plan's Join operator gains a
151	``strategy`` field of ``HASH`` or ``SORT_MERGE``.  A JOIN-less statement
152	accepts either strategy but gains no extra operator, and an invalid
153	strategy raises :class:`ValueError` before any source file is opened.
154	"""
155

227	def _validate_join_strategy(join_strategy: Any) -> str | None:
228	    """Validate the optional ``join_strategy`` argument.
229	
230	    Returns the canonical lowercase strategy name, or ``None`` when the
231	    caller did not request one.  Any other value (including a non-string)
232	    raises :class:`ValueError`; callers run this before opening any file.
233	    """
234	    if join_strategy is None:
235	        return None
236	    if not isinstance(join_strategy, str) or join_strategy not in _JOIN_STRATEGIES:
237	        allowed = ", ".join(sorted(_JOIN_STRATEGIES))
238	        raise ValueError(
239	            f"invalid join_strategy: {join_strategy!r}; expected one of {allowed}"
240	        )

244	class QuerySyntaxError(Exception):
245	    """Raised when a query is lexically or grammatically invalid."""

249	    """Raised when a syntactically valid query is incompatible with the schema."""

252	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
253	# Tokeniser
254	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
255	
256	
257	@dataclass(frozen=True)
258	class _Token:
259	    kind: str  # one of: keyword, ident, number, string, op, star, eof
260	    value: Any
261	    text: str
262	
263	
264	_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(
265	    r"""
266	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
267	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5
268	    """,
269	    re.VERBOSE,
270	)
271	# Bare identifiers: Unicode letters/underscore first, then word characters.
272	_IDENT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\W\d]\w*", re.UNICODE)
273	
274	
275	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
276	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
277	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
278	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
279	    i = 0
280	    n = len(sql)
281	    while i < n:
282	        ch = sql[i]
283	        if ch.isspace():
284	            i += 1
285	            continue
286	        if ch == "*":
287	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
288	            i += 1
289	            continue
290	        if ch in ",()+-/":
291	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
292	            i += 1
293	            continue
294	        if ch in "=<>!":
295	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
296	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
297	                i += 2
298	                continue
299	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
300	                op = ch + "="
301	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
302	                i += 2
303	                continue
304	            if ch in "=<>":
305	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
306	                i += 1
307	                continue
308	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
309	        if ch == "'":
310	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
311	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
312	            i = new_i
313	            continue
314	        if ch == '"':
315	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
316	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
317	            i = new_i
318	            continue
319	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
320	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
321	            if match:
322	                text = match.group(0)
323	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
324	                i = match.end()
325	                continue
326	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
327	            # used by two-table queries ("table.column").
328	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
329	            i += 1
330	            continue
331	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
332	        if match:
333	            text = match.group(0)
334	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
335	            i = match.end()
336	            continue
337	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
338	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
339	    return tokens

342	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
343	    lowered = word.lower()
344	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
345	        if lowered == "true":
346	            return _Token("number", True, word)
347	        if lowered == "false":
348	            return _Token("number", False, word)
349	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
350	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)

352	
353	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
354	    parts: list[str] = []
355	    i = start + 1
356	    n = len(sql)
357	    while True:
358	        j = sql.find("'", i)
359	        if j == -1:
360	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
361	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
362	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
363	            parts.append("'")
364	            i = j + 2
365	            continue
366	        value = "".join(parts)
367	        try:
368	            value.encode("utf-8")
369	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
370	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
371	        return value, j + 1
372	
373	
374	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
375	    parts: list[str] = []
376	    i = start + 1
377	    n = len(sql)
378	    while True:
379	        j = sql.find('"', i)
380	        if j == -1:
381	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
382	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
383	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
384	            parts.append('"')
385	            i = j + 2
386	            continue
387	        value = "".join(parts)
388	        if not value:
389	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
390	        return value, j + 1
391	
392	
393	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
394	    try:
395	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
396	            value: int | float = float(text)
397	        else:
398	            value = int(text, 10)
399	    except ValueError:
400	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
401	    if isinstance(value, int):
402	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
403	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
404	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
405	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
406	        return value
407	    if not math.isfinite(value):
408	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
409	    return value

417	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
418	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
419	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
420	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
421	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
422	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
423	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
424	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
425	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
426	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
427	#   ("not", operand)
428	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
429	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
430	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
431	#
432	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
433	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
434	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'

498	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):

513	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:

575	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
576	        tok = self._peek()

580	            )

594	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
595	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
596	        while self._accept_op(","):
597	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
598	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
599	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
600	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
601	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
602	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
603	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
604	        tok = self._peek()
605	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
606	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
607	        ):

609	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
610	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
611	            )

613	                raise QueryValidationError(

615	                )

619	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
620	        tok = self._peek()
621	        if tok.kind == "star":
622	            self._next()
623	            return _RefItem("star")
624	        if (
625	            tok.kind == "ident"
626	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
627	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
628	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("

630	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
631	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
632	                raise QueryValidationError(
633	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
634	                )

636	        node = self._parse_arith()
637	        if node[0] == "column":

639	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
640	            return _RefItem(
641	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
642	            )

644	        self._expect_keyword("as")
645	        alias = self._peek()

647	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
648	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
649	            )

711	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
712	        tok = self._peek()

714	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")

729	        self._expect_op(")")

731	            "agg",

738	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
739	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
740	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
741	        # name "" stands for '*'.

744	            raise QueryValidationError(

746	            )

748	            if func != "count":

752	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
753	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
754	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
755	            )

757	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
758	            nxt = self._peek()
759	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
760	                raise QuerySyntaxError(

762	                )

764	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
765	        self._next()
766	        nxt = self._peek()
767	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
768	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
769	                raise QueryValidationError(
770	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
771	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
772	                )
773	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
774	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
775	            )
